title: Dispatch: finding registry v1 (attempt 1)
description:
SUPERVISOR PRE-PLANNING. Implement exactly what is specified here. Read the
parent spec first: `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.1.6`.

=== WHY THIS IS URGENT ===
The registry is the instrument that keeps the repairs honest. If it is assembled
near closure it cannot govern the repairs it exists to govern. Nine
implementation beads are blocked on this one.

=== FILES YOU OWN ===
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/finding-registry.json
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/finding-registry.md
  packages/core/src/rules/findingRegistry.ts
  packages/core/test/findingRegistry.test.ts
Do NOT edit package.json, packages/core/package.json, or
packages/core/src/internal.ts. npm-script and CI wiring is explicitly the job of
eshyra-o9bd.19.1.5, not this bead; your test invokes the validator directly by
relative import ('../src/rules/findingRegistry.js').

=== WHERE THE FINDINGS COME FROM ===
Two sources, both readable from this machine:

1. /mnt/d/eshyra-2026-07-24-audit-repair-bead-plan.md — read it in full. The
   per-review finding lists are in the sections titled "Independent Sol audit",
   "Opus 5 original audit", "Opus 5 amended creature/magic-item audit",
   "GPT-5.6-Sol agent audit", and "Fable 5 audit" (roughly lines 582-682), plus
   "Magic-item capability families", "Partial and unimplemented rule
   procedures", and "Design-blocked rules already claiming owners".
2. The bead tree: `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19` and every descendant, plus
   eshyra-olc5 and its descendants. Most beads carry an explicit
   "Closes findings: ..." line. Those lines are the authority for the
   owning-bead column.

=== REGISTRY v1 SHAPE (one row per canonical defect or invariant) ===
  canonicalId          one stable ID you assign
  aliases[]            EVERY alias from EVERY review, each fully qualified
  title                one line
  status               accepted | rejected | narrowed | ambiguous |
                       disclosed-dependency
  statusReasoning      required whenever status is not "accepted"
  membershipQuery      the NAME of a generated query implemented in
                       findingRegistry.ts — never a stored count, never a
                       hand-copied total
  owningBead           an existing bead ID
  packBoundary         what the pack must represent
  engineBoundary       which engine:F* capability, or "none"
  regressionForm       the intended shape of the permanent regression evidence

=== DISPUTED AND NON-LITERAL FINDINGS — get these exactly right ===
* sol:CAP-002 (condition/action/feat structural gaps) must be PRESENT and marked
  NARROWED, never implemented literally. The 2026-07-24 independent audit
  verified conditions as EXACT against source; implementing CAP-002 literally
  would REGRESS already-correct typed condition effects. The row must state the
  no-regression requirement on existing typed condition effects.
* The Fable language-set conclusion is an ADJUDICATION / POLICY question, not a
  projection defect. Status it accordingly, not as "accepted".
* Conflicting counts across reviews — 79 vs 77 creature half-damage, 8 vs 9
  hazard, 391 vs 399 engine:F5 — must resolve to a GENERATED MEMBERSHIP QUERY.
  Never reconcile them by choosing a number. The disagreement itself is
  evidence that stored totals are untrustworthy; say so on the row.

=== packages/core/src/rules/findingRegistry.ts ===
  * loads and schema-validates the JSON;
  * implements the named membership queries against the committed pack at
    packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/records.json (records
    use the `key` field, NOT `id`; executionReadiness lives at
    `record.data.executionReadiness`, not `record.executionReadiness`);
  * exposes an alias index and detects (a) an alias resolving to two rows,
    (b) an unqualified alias, (c) a row whose membershipQuery names an
    unimplemented query, (d) a row carrying a hard-coded total;
  * exposes a bead-reference check that SKIPS gracefully when the `bd` binary
    is unavailable, in the style of the repo's dolt-gated tests — do not make
    the suite depend on bd being installed.

=== packages/core/test/findingRegistry.test.ts ===
  * the registry validates against its schema;
  * every alias from every review resolves to exactly ONE canonical row;
  * no row carries a hand-copied total;
  * every membershipQuery name is implemented and executes against the real pack;
  * sol:CAP-002 is present, status narrowed, and its row states the
    no-regression requirement;
  * every non-accepted status carries reasoning.

=== finding-registry.md ===
A human-readable companion: how to add a row, what each status means, why
membership queries replace counts, and the alias prefix table. Keep the JSON the
single source of truth — the .md must not restate row data that could drift.

=== NAMING HAZARD — READ BEFORE WRITING ANY IDENTIFIER ===
"F1".."F10" means THREE different things in this repository:
  engine:F1..F10    pack executionReadiness engineHooks[].engine families
  fable:F1..F8      Fable 5 audit findings
  opus:F-01..F-35   Opus 5 audit findings
  sol:CAP-001..014  GPT-5.6-Sol agent audit findings
  indep:001..012    independent review findings (renamed from SOL-*)
Never write a bare "F5" or a bare "CAP-002". Always qualify with the prefix.
The CLOSED epic eshyra-2n1t used yet another F1-F10 taxonomy that does NOT
correspond to engine:F1-F10 except loosely at F2/F3/F5/F7.

=== COUNT HYGIENE ===
No test and no committed artifact may depend on a hand-copied number (391, 399,
77, 79, 794, 1016, 1813). Every count is a SNAPSHOT of commit 4384f25. Where a
count matters, commit the QUERY that generates it and let the number be derived
at run time.

=== ENVIRONMENT AND VERIFICATION ===
Run `npm ci` in this worktree FIRST. Worktrees have no node_modules of their
own and will otherwise resolve @eshyra/core through the parent checkout's stale
dist/*.d.ts and report phantom typecheck errors.
Then run `npm run verify:worktree` BEFORE committing — it rewrites files
(Biome formats and organizes imports), so verifying after committing means the
committed tree is not the tree that passed.

=== HARD CONSTRAINTS ===
* Edit ONLY the files listed under "FILES YOU OWN". Two sibling dispatches are
  running in parallel right now on disjoint file sets. Touching anything else —
  especially package.json, packages/core/package.json, or
  packages/core/src/internal.ts — will collide with them. If you believe you
  need a file outside your list, record that in your completion notes instead
  and stop short of editing it.
* Do NOT modify any bead except your own. Do NOT run `bd dolt push`. If you
  discover follow-up work, use `bd create` and say so in your notes.
* Do NOT push, do NOT open or comment on a pull request, do NOT merge.
  AGENTS.md's standing push authority does not apply to you on this dispatch;
  integration belongs to the agent that dispatched you. Committed work on your
  branch is a complete handoff.
* Do NOT weaken, skip, or delete any existing test or audit expectation.
* Do NOT regenerate the rules pack and do NOT run the SRD importer.
acceptance_criteria:
• Registry v1 is checked in and populated for every finding across all four reviews.
• Every row carries a generated membership query; no row carries a hand-copied total.
• Every alias from every review resolves to exactly one canonical row.
• Disputed findings carry an explicit non-accepted status with recorded reasoning.
• sol:CAP-002 present, marked narrowed, with the no-regression requirement stated.
• Tests execute the membership queries against the committed pack and pass.
• npm run verify:worktree passes from this worktree.
• No file outside the owned list is modified.
